_comment: THE CACHE CONTRACT A PUBLISHED INSTANCE IS CHECKED AGAINST, AS DATA.
WHAT IS NORMATIVE IS NOT HERE. Static-Site-Architecture.md §2.9 is the object-class
registry and says so about itself; Publishing-And-Caching.md §4 states that its own table
is GENERATED from §2.9 and that `where this table and the registry disagree, the registry
is normative and this one is stale`. This file is a THIRD copy, and it is the one a
program reads. That is a transcription, and a transcription that nobody can re-derive is
a number and not a check — so `source` below records the specs commit and the sha256 of
each section's exact text as transcribed, and `tools/verify/cache-policy-drift.mjs`
recomputes both against a `codetracer-specs` checkout.
THE DRIFT GUARD CANNOT RUN IN CI AND THAT RESIDUAL IS RECORDED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER.
`codetracer-specs` is not checked out by `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `Justfile`'s
`snapshot-contract-tables` recipe records the same limitation for the same reason. So the
guard is an operator command (`just cache-policy-drift`), it REFUSES when it cannot find a
checkout rather than passing, and the CI step that exists is the one that can run offline:
that this file parses, that its rows are ordered specific-before-general, and that every
row is reachable by at least one key (an unreachable row is a rule that can never fire).
ORDER IS PART OF THE DATA. `match` patterns are tried in order and the FIRST hit wins, so
`d/*/current.json` must precede `d/**` and `src/*/*/current.json` must precede `src/**`.
A registry whose order is wrong does not fail loudly — it silently applies the general
rule to the specific object, which for `current.json` means asserting a year of
immutability on the one hot mutable object per chain. `orderSanity` below is the list of
(key, expected row id) pairs that pins the order; the selftest drives every one.
PATTERN LANGUAGE, deliberately tiny so it can be read as well as matched:
`*`  matches exactly one path segment (no `/`)
`**` matches the remainder, including `/`, and may only appear last
everything else is literal. Keys are tree-relative with no leading slash, which is how
`publisher.nim`'s `classOf` and `objectstore.nim`'s listings both spell them.
THE CHAIN SLUG IN `orderSanity` IS `some-chain` AND NOT A REAL ONE, deliberately. These pins
are about PATTERN ORDER — `*` matches any one segment — and a real slug in them would read as
though the matcher knew something about that chain. Aztec is the first chain this runs
against and nothing here knows that.
ONE §2.9 ROW IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT: `/ops/**`, whose Cache column reads `not public`. That
is not a cache rule — it is an exposure rule, and the right check is `this prefix must not be
served at all`, which belongs beside the INSTRUMENT control rather than in a table of
`Cache-Control` values. It is recorded here rather than left as a silent omission, because a
row missing from a transcription and a row that does not exist look the same in review.
`expect` FIELDS ARE ASSERTIONS ABOUT DIRECTIVES, NOT ABOUT THE HEADER STRING. Two
byte-different `Cache-Control` values can state the same policy (order, spacing, a
`public` that some CDNs add). So each row states the directives that must be present with
the values they must have, and `forbid` names directives that must be ABSENT — which is
how `no-store` on a `/t/` 404 is distinguished from `no-store` plus a `max-age` nobody
meant.

sections.note: §4 states that it is generated from §2.9 and stale where the two disagree.

rows.why: The only hot mutable object per chain (§2.9: Mutable=yes, selects the generation).
Moves when a better source match lands (§2.9: Mutable=yes).
Content-addressed bundle bytes (§2.9: identity = bundle bytes, Mutable=no).
A sealed generation, root included (§2.9: Mutable=no, generation member).
Immutable facts keyed by entity hash or by address+range — block, tx, ts, seg (§2.9).
Permanent traces keyed by traceArtifactId (§2.9, §4). Windowed objects carry a different policy SET BY THE OBJECT, not by the path — see `windowedException`.
Version in the path or in meta.json (§2.9: Mutable=no, while referenced).
Content-hashed release assets (§2.9: identity = content hash, SRI).
Version in the filename; short TTL for pointer freshness (§2.9: 300 s + SWR).
Generation member, crawler-facing (§2.9: 1y immutable, while referenced).
Release visibility (§2.9 entry pages: route identity, 60 s + SWR).

absent.why: A cached 404 outlives the generation or renewal the client is polling for (Deployment §4.1). This is the single cache rule whose absence is a correctness defect rather than a tuning one, and it is Cloudflare's DEFAULT that is wrong: an unconfigured zone caches 404s for three minutes.
